items.explanation: Kataba has no weak letter. Qāla (q-w-l) and ramā (r-m-y) are weak.

options: A wāw, yāʾ or alif among its root letters
items.explanation: The weak letters are wāw, yāʾ and alif; a hamza does not make a verb weak.

items.prompt: What do the books call this verb (he stretched)?
options: muḍāʿaf: its second and third letters are the same
sālim: no hamza and no doubled letter
muʿtall: it has a weak letter
items.explanation: Madda comes from m-d-d: the second and third root letters are the same.
